studies.title: Making Decentralisation Work: A Handbook for Policy-Makers
studies.design: comparative synthesis of empirical research and country experience
studies.summary: Decentralisation can support efficiency, accountability and regional development, but outcomes depend strongly on design, sequencing, capacity, fiscal arrangements and coordination. The report explicitly rejects treating decentralisation as a panacea.
studies.caveats: Not a meta-analysis; combines empirical studies with comparative institutional evidence, and findings are context-dependent.

studies.title: Evaluation of devolved institutions
studies.authors: Warwick Economics and Development for BEIS
studies.design: mixed-method evaluation of mayoral combined authorities, Cornwall and London
studies.summary: Examines how English devolved institutions operate, including leadership, governance, partnership working and perceptions. It is useful for institutional mechanisms but was not designed to estimate long-run causal effects on growth or public-service outcomes.
studies.caveats: Small perception surveys and institutional/process focus limit causal attribution.

studies.title: Devolution in England: funding and accountability
studies.design: audit of funding, accountability and implementation arrangements
studies.summary: Finds that the accountability framework for English devolution is still developing, that local accountability must be strengthened and tested, and that future local and central capacity are material implementation risks.
studies.caveats: Assesses arrangements and risks rather than estimating causal impacts of devolution on outcomes.

studies.title: Governance of place-based policies now and in the future
studies.summary: Identifies multi-level coordination, strategic and technical capacity, fiscal capacity, place leadership and inclusive engagement as recurring governance conditions for effective place-based policy.
studies.caveats: Strong on recurring mechanisms and implementation conditions; weaker for estimating a single average causal effect.

studies.title: Decentralization of Health and Education in Developing Countries: A Quality-Adjusted Review of the Empirical Literature
studies.design: review weighting quantitative evidence by identification quality
studies.summary: Higher-quality studies in the reviewed literature generally indicate gains in technical efficiency from decentralisation and some improvement in preference matching, although effects are conditional and evidence remains uneven.
studies.caveats: Transferability to contemporary English institutions is indirect; service sectors and country settings differ.

studies.title: Decentralization and Governance
studies.design: review of governance mechanisms and empirical literature
studies.summary: Synthesises mechanisms through which decentralisation may improve accountability and responsiveness, while also noting risks including fiscal weakness and capture.
studies.caveats: Mechanism-focused rather than a pooled causal estimate; institutional transferability matters.

studies.title: Fiscal decentralization and economic growth reconsidered
studies.summary: When fiscal decentralisation is measured using revenues over which subnational governments have genuine autonomy, the estimated association with economic growth is not statistically significant.
studies.caveats: Cross-country observational design; limited sample; does not rule out indirect or context-specific growth channels.

studies.title: Is fiscal decentralization harmful for economic growth? Evidence from the OECD countries
studies.summary: Reports a negative association between fiscal decentralisation and growth in the sample, while political and administrative decentralisation effects are weaker and sensitive to measurement.
studies.caveats: Observational cross-country evidence; measurement of decentralisation and endogeneity remain important concerns.

studies.title: Fiscal Decentralization and Economic Growth
studies.design: review of theoretical and empirical growth literature
studies.summary: Concludes that the direct growth effect of fiscal decentralisation remained an open empirical question and that indirect channels were under-developed in the literature.
studies.caveats: Older evidence base; useful mainly as a benchmark showing persistent uncertainty in the direct growth channel.

studies.title: Local government revenue decentralisation and funding divergence: an English case study
studies.authors: Neil Amin Smith, David Phillips and Polly Simpson
studies.type: English fiscal modelling / empirical case study
studies.design: historical analysis and simulation of local government finance reforms
studies.summary: Shows that greater reliance on local revenue can recreate substantial fiscal disparities even after initial equalisation, with outcomes highly sensitive to equalisation and revenue-sharing design.
studies.caveats: Examines fiscal resources and incentives rather than downstream service or growth outcomes.

studies.title: Taking control: which taxes could be devolved to English local government?
studies.authors: Neil Amin Smith, Tom Harris and David Phillips
studies.summary: Finds that additional tax devolution can increase local discretion and incentives, but creates trade-offs around volatility, inequality, administration and redistribution and is not a solution to overall funding adequacy.
studies.caveats: Primarily ex ante institutional and fiscal analysis rather than causal evaluation.

studies.title: Decentralization and Service Delivery
studies.authors: Junaid Ahmad, Shantayanan Devarajan, Stuti Khemani and Shekhar Shah
studies.summary: Explains why decentralisation can improve service delivery when citizen-to-politician and politician-to-provider accountability relationships are strong, and why it can fail when those accountability chains are weak.
studies.caveats: Older and largely developing-country evidence; best treated as mechanism evidence, not direct proof for England.

studies.title: Introducing Integrated Care Systems: joining up local services to improve health outcomes
studies.design: audit of system setup, risks and prerequisites
studies.summary: Finds a credible rationale for local integration and prevention but stresses that workforce, finance, relationships, objectives and implementation capacity are prerequisites; the report did not yet judge value for money or outcome impact.
studies.caveats: Early-stage assessment, not an impact evaluation.

studies.title: Making decentralisation work: transparency, data and performance monitoring
studies.design: review of transparency and monitoring evidence plus institutional guidance
studies.summary: Synthesises evidence that transparency can strengthen accountability, participation and public financial management, while recommending simple, reliable performance-monitoring systems and information with clear territorial relevance.
studies.caveats: The transparency evidence spans multiple public-sector contexts and does not isolate English devolution effects.

studies.title: Place Based Budgets
studies.summary: Five pilots are testing whether coordinated place-based funding and decision-making can improve services, collaboration and prevention. The programme is explicitly designed to generate evidence on feasibility, effectiveness and scalability through 2029.
studies.caveats: No completed outcome evidence yet; this is evidence of an active test and therefore a live gap rather than evidence of effect.
